facts.text: Grantsville was founded in 1785 when Daniel Grant bought 1,100 acres called Cornucopia, and the town was named after him.
The Casselman Bridge, a historic stone arch bridge, sits just north of Grantsville and has been a landmark since the 19th century.
The Grantsville Community Museum on Main Street showcases a vast photography collection by Leo Beachy, documenting local life from 1905 to 1927.
In 1872, Garrett County was carved out of Allegany County and named after John Work Garrett, president of the B&O Railroad.
The Casselman Inn, established in 1824, has served travelers on the National Road for nearly two centuries.
Every June, Grantsville hosts the Grantsville Days festival, featuring fireworks, a parade, live music, crafts, and a classic car show.
